title: On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations - a Dezornification
version: arXiv:1309.7591v3 (2 Jul 2015); published Ann. Henri Poincaré, DOI 10.1007/s00023-015-0401-5
sections_read: Abstract; §1 incl. footnote 3; Definition 2.1 (GHD), 2.2-2.4 (extension, CGHD), Remark 2.5; Theorems 2.6, 2.7 (global uniqueness), 2.8 (existence/uniqueness of MGHD), 3.4 (MCGHD); §1.5 gluing discussion incl. non-Hausdorff 'corresponding boundary points' mechanism
assumptions: Vacuum Einstein equations; initial data on a manifold M-bar; development must embed M-bar as a Cauchy surface (Definition 2.1 condition 3)
conclusion: Existence and uniqueness up to isometry of the maximal globally hyperbolic development, for full Cauchy data; two GHDs of the same data admit a common GHD extension
proof_status: authors' claims, established result; proof read selectively (Zorn-free gluing construction)
relevance: Primary source for the scope of the MGHD framework: it does NOT contain premise (L') of SCREENING.md; Definition 2.1(3) positively requires Cauchy embedding, so partial hypersurfaces like K1 or h(K1) fall outside it
limits: Full-data theorem only; the localized partial-hypersurface statement is absent; proof read selectively, not line-audited
open_questions: Does D-agreement (RESULT.md L'') for partial spacelike acausal data follow from Sbierski's gluing restricted to the domain of dependence?

title: Global aspects of the Cauchy problem in general relativity
assumptions: Constraint-satisfying initial data on a hypersurface; developments with a Cauchy surface
conclusion: Per abstract: 'Any solution of Einstein's equations which has a Cauchy surface may be embedded in exactly one such maximal development'
relevance: Origin of the MGHD theorem; confirms the framework quantifies over solutions 'which have a Cauchy surface', i.e. full-data scope

title: Further results on the smoothability of Cauchy hypersurfaces and Cauchy time functions
version: arXiv:gr-qc/0512095 (submitted 15 Dec 2005); Lett. Math. Phys., DOI 10.1007/s11005-006-0091-5
sections_read: Definition paragraph (Cauchy hypersurface = crossed exactly once by every inextendible timelike curve; then at least once by any inextendible causal curve; achronal, not always acausal; spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces necessarily acausal); Theorem 1.1; Theorem 1.2; Proposition 3.6; Example 3.4 reference; Remark 4.14; Theorem 5.15
assumptions: Time-oriented globally hyperbolic spacetime; submanifolds smooth, spacelike, acausal; Theorem 1.1 requires compactness (with boundary)
conclusion: Thm 1.1: compact spacelike acausal submanifold with boundary extends to a spacelike Cauchy hypersurface (non-connected case Remark 4.14); if only achronal, smooth extension fails in general (Example 3.4). Thm 1.2/5.15: Cauchy temporal functions with prescribed levels exist
proof_status: authors' claims; statements read, proofs selectively (not line-audited)
relevance: Fixes the Cauchy-surface convention under which SCREENING.md Theorem 2's C0 boundary-of-past-set construction is a legitimate Cauchy hypersurface; its compactness gate is why route 'h(K1) lies in a Cauchy surface of M2' is blocked for noncompact K1
limits: Compact-only extension; no noncompact acausal-extension theorem located anywhere (and the hyperbola example shows none can hold in general)
